member.name: T:SysWeaver.FileMetaData
member.summary: Tools for associating meta data (and derived files, such as compressed copies) with the content of a file, and rebuild it when the file has changed.
member.remarks: Meta data is keyed by the content hash of the file (see ), so identical files share meta data and any change invalidates it. The meta data is stored as gzip compressed json in a folder per key type (configurable using "FileMetaDataFolders" and "FileMetaData[KeyType]Folders" in the config), and is pruned at process exit when it hasn't been used for the configured number of days. Processing of a given content hash is serialized across processes using a keyed by the key type, the key suffix and the content hash, so a process callback may process the same content using another key type or key suffix (ex: using on the same file), but processing the same content with the same key type and key suffix from inside a callback dead locks (the lock isn't re-entrant). The key type folder is created on first use (per process); if it's deleted while the process is running, it's re-created when a write to it fails with a (the failed process callback or meta data write is retried once).

member.name: T:SysWeaver.KeyValueStore
member.summary: Represent a file based key value store. Prefer using the Async methods if possible. Designed to be as reliable as possible, not for speed: - Uses system wide locks (, one per key) for data read/writes, so it's safe to use from multiple threads and processes. - Uses redundancy by having R copies of the data (one file per copy, in separate sub folders and optionally on separate volumes). - Uses a SHA256 checksum to validate the data (detects corruption, invalid copies are deleted when found). - Compresses data (save disc space). When setting data: - The oldest copies (non-existing and invalid copies count as very old) are overwritten with the new data. When reading data: - The most recent valid copy is returned.
member.remarks: The key is used as the file name of the copies, so it MUST be a valid file name: not null or empty, not "." or "..", and no invalid file name chars (no path separators or ':', on Windows also no '*', '?', '"', '<', '>', '|' or control chars), i.e. must return the key unchanged. This is validated in all builds, an is thrown for invalid keys (so a key can't be used to access files outside the store). Keys are never transformed, since changing the file name would make existing data unreadable: callers that build keys from arbitrary text must make them valid file names (ex: using ). Values are written with the configured serializer, so the same type should be used when reading. Not intended for large values or high write rates, every operation touches all copies.

member.name: F:SysWeaver.KeyValueStore.UserApp
member.summary: A default key/value store that is unique to the user but application specific, stored in .
member.remarks: Legacy fallback (applies to , and ): Before 2026-10-07 these stores were the same instance as , so existing data is in the location. Deleting a key from this store stops the fallback for that key (a marker is written), but doesn't delete the copy. Note: is common to all users, so (as before) a value written to a per user store by older versions is visible to all users until it's set in their own store. member.name: T:SysWeaver.SystemLock
member.summary: System wide (cross process) named locks, implemented using exclusively opened lock files (delete on close) so they work on all OS'es.
member.remarks: The lock file name is an MD5 hash of the key, stored in the "SystemLock" . Locks are NOT re-entrant, taking the same lock twice from the same thread / async flow will dead lock. Waiting is done by polling every 10 ms (no fairness). A lock object that isn't disposed is released by its finalizer. On Unix the exclusivity relies on advisory file locking, so all participants must use this class. On Unix a lock file is only considered taken if the opened file is still the one linked at the path (a waiter may open the old file just before the previous holder unlinks it), and the holder unlinks the path before closing the file (it's not opened with delete on close).

member.returns: A lock object, dispose to unlock
member.exception: Opening the lock file failed with a non IO exception (ex: access denied) more than 10 times.
